meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/05, Thursday 15 May 2025). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: THIS is OCR's non-calculator Higher paper, not paper 4. Higher partner of J560/02. 100 marks, read from the [N] part markers in the QP margin.

coding_notes: TIER CROSSOVER: q1, q2, q5, q6, q8 and q9 are the same questions as J560/02 q15, q16, q18, q19, q21 and q24, with identical marks and identical tags. q7a is a near-twin of J560/02 q20 (draw a line to solve a pair of simultaneous equations) but uses different equations and carries an extra part, so it is coded separately.

q11 (is a 10 cm cube of steel plausible, by estimation) tagged compound_units + estimating + volume_of_a_prism: density supplies the compound unit, the mark scheme rewards rounding 7.9 to 8, and the cube's volume is the bridge. There is no cube-root node, and none of the three is a good sole tag.
q13 (p proportional to the square root of m) tagged proportion_with_powers — a root is a power, and the node's example is the same shape of problem.

q17b (error interval for the RANGE of grouped masses) tagged range + upper_and_lower_bounds. Neither alone covers it: the grouped intervals fix the bounds and the range is what those bounds are placed on.
q21a (state the assumption behind multiplying two identical probabilities) tagged combined_events — the assumption IS independence, which is that node's content.

q21b (probability about the contents of a bag after two sweets are eaten) tagged tree_diagrams rather than conditional_probability: the mark scheme's method is products along branches with a changing denominator, and tree_diagrams credits four skills where conditional_probability credits seven.
q22 tagged cosine_rule + area_of_triangle_sine. The exact value of sin 45 also earns a mark, but exact_trig_values was left off rather than credit a third skill for one mark.
